transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-04
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Claire Mendoza (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Arboretum Head of Platform), Luis Ortega (Arboretum Lead ML), Priya Rao (Arboretum Security), Tom Bolton (CTO)

Summary:
Arboretum is evaluating Redwood for a mixed deployment: hosted for low-latency consumer-facing features, Dedicated for steady throughput, and a Private/VPC option for regulated pipelines. Primary engineering questions focused on SDK integration (JS/Python), adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy patterns for on-prem, how rate limiting and quotas surface to clients, and what observability hooks (OpenTelemetry/Jaeger/trace ids) Redwood exposes. Security touched on KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2 artifacts. Next steps: bench, security packet, and follow-up pilot kickoff.

Topics discussed:
- SDK quickstart, LangChain + LlamaIndex adapters
- Gateway / proxy vs sidecar vs direct SDK calls
- Rate-limits: per-token, per-route, global quota semantics
- Observability: traces, per-request token/cost metrics, logs/retention
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Claire Mendoza: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, great to meet you all. We're Claire at Redwood, AE. Uh, quick round of intros?
[00:10] Maya Chen: Hi I'm Maya, Head of Platform at Arboretum. We run a mixed fleet — some cloud microservices, a few on-prem data pipelines.
[00:18] Tom Bolton: Tom, CTO, focused on architecture and compliance.
[00:22] Luis Ortega: Luis, lead ML eng, I'll be hands-on for the pilot.
[00:25] Priya Rao: Priya, security, I'll be the compliance reviewer.
[00:29] Devon Park: Devon here, Redwood SE, I usually do the integration and bench stuff.
[00:33] Claire Mendoza: Cool, thanks. High level Arboretum goal: embed a set of LLM features in our search and docs product — some low latency chat, embeddings for semantic search, and a nightly batch reranker. We saw your doc on Dedicated pools and Private VPC so wanted to align on integration model and operations.
[00:50] Maya Chen: Right, and our primary constraints are: one, data residency for PII pipelines; two, predictable unit economics for high-traffic flows; three, instrumentability — we need fine grained metrics.
[01:02] Devon Park: Makes sense. For SDKs we support Python and Node — we have sample quickstarts. Are you using LangChain or LlamaIndex in your stack?
[01:10] Luis Ortega: We're mostly LangChain for orchestration, but some teams use LlamaIndex on the search path. We need both adapters to be easy to drop in.
[01:18] Devon Park: Great — Redwood's SDK has first-class LangChain connectors, and the community LlamaIndex adapter is maintained in the repo. Small caveat: the adapter naming in the docs sometimes spells LlamaIndex as llama-index or Llama Index, so our quickstart has exact import snippets.
[01:32] Luis Ortega: Ha yeah, we've hit that typo before. For LlamaIndex, do you preserve chunk-level metadata so we can do selective retrieval?
[01:40] Devon Park: Yes, retrieval is passthrough; the embedding pipeline tags vectors with original chunk IDs. We also surface the vector-id in response metadata so downstream services can re-hydrate.
[01:52] Priya Rao: From security perspective, how does the gateway/proxy option look? We can't push certain data out directly to hosted endpoints without encrypting keys in KMS.
[02:00] Claire Mendoza: Two patterns: 1) direct SDK calls from services into Redwood-hosted endpoints with VPC peering and private networking for Private deployments, or 2) a gateway/proxy sidecar you run — that can be used with Dedicated or Private. The sidecar handles local auth, credential injection, and rate-limit enforcement locally.
[02:18] Tom Bolton: If we run a sidecar on-prem, how do we handle model upgrades or rollbacks? We don't want to patch a fleet manually.
[02:26] Devon Park: Good question. For Dedicated/Private we push runtime configs from the Redwood control plane. Sidecars pull a signed manifest and support canary rollouts per cluster. You can pin model versions per route so rollouts are controlled.
[02:40] Maya Chen: What about observability — we need trace IDs through the whole pipeline. Can Redwood propagate trace context so we can stitch together traces in our Jaeger?
[02:49] Devon Park: Yes, we support OpenTelemetry headers. Outgoing responses include trace-id and we can export spans to your OTLP collector (self-hosted or vendor). We also provide per-request token and cost metrics as tags.
[03:03] Maya Chen: Per-request token costs as tags? So I can see cost per API call in our traces?
[03:07] Devon Park: Correct — token_count, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and cost_usd are available as attributes. That helps for SLO and cost allocations.
[03:16] Luis Ortega: That's useful. For rate-limits: do you expose headers like X-RateLimit-Remaining or do clients need to call a separate quota API?
[03:24] Devon Park: We expose standard headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset) for the hosted API. For Dedicated we support both headers and a telemetry endpoint that returns quota usage per key. For Private, you can surface those locally via the sidecar.
[03:41] Priya Rao: And quotas can be defined per-customer, per-route, and per-model?
[03:45] Claire Mendoza: Yes, policies are flexible: per-api-key, per-route, per-model, and global account caps. We can also configure burst windows separately from steady-state RPM.
[03:55] Tom Bolton: We're also worried about cold-start latencies for occasional large requests. Do you have KV cache warmup or prefix caching?
[04:04] Devon Park: Our runtime supports KV-cache warmup and prefix caching; for large batched workloads we recommend Dedicated with pre-warmed workers. The control plane can prefetch common prompts into cache on rollout.
[04:17] Luis Ortega: On the topic of cost: what's the unit economics for a dedicated pool vs hosted? Ballpark figures to budget.
[04:24] Claire Mendoza: I'll send the exact pricing sheet but rough: hosted pay-as-you-go is higher per-token but no infra commitments. Dedicated has a monthly commit and lowers per-token inference costs significantly. Private has a base platform fee plus infra. We'll attach a spreadsheet.
[04:38] Maya Chen: For the pilot we want to test three flows: 1) low-latency chat on hosted, 2) batch reranker on Dedicated, and 3) PII-handling pipeline on Private/VPC. Can Redwood support running those in parallel?
[04:51] Devon Park: Absolutely — routing policy can route requests by tag: 'latency' -> hosted, 'batch' -> dedicated, 'sensitive' -> private. We can demo routing rules in the pilot.
[05:02] Priya Rao: On KMS: Can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS or an HSM? We need keys never visible to Redwood control plane for certain data.
[05:10] Devon Park: We have KMS integrations for hosted customers using a Customer-Managed Key (CMK) via AWS IAM roles. For the strictest requirements we offer a private deployment with HSM-backed key material, where the key operations are performed in customer-managed VPC.
[05:24] Priya Rao: Audit logs: retention and export options?
[05:28] Claire Mendoza: Audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has audit events but retention is shorter unless you add the compliance pack. We can stream logs to your S3/GCS or to a SIEM via secure forwarder.
[05:40] Luis Ortega: On the SDK experience — latency on small chat messages is important. Is there a websocket streaming option?
[05:45] Devon Park: Yes, streaming via websockets or SSE for both hosted and dedicated. Private supports streaming too but depends on your proxy configuration. The JS SDK auto-reconnects and resumes token streaming where supported.
[05:58] Maya Chen: A few gotchas we've seen: LangChain chain-of-thought prompts can leak context if KV cache isn't invalidated properly. Is cache eviction deterministic?
[06:08] Devon Park: Eviction policies are tunable: time-based TTLs, LRU, and manual invalidation via API. For sensitive workloads we recommend not caching full prompts and instead caching only embeddings or non-PII artifacts.
[06:22] Tom Bolton: We run internal traffic shaping — is there a way to have Redwood signal backpressure so our gateway can shed load?
[06:29] Devon Park: We have per-route congestion backoff headers and a 'queue-length' metric in the response for Dedicated, so your gateway can implement circuit-breaking.
[06:38] Luis Ortega: For LlamaIndex adapter, can we store retrieved node ids and pass them back to the model for streaming re-rank?
[06:45] Devon Park: Yes, retrieval metadata is preserved and passed as structured tool-calls in streaming responses. There can be small differences between LangChain and LlamaIndex payload formats; our adapter normalizes them.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Onboarding time — how long to get pilot up and running? We're aiming for pilot week of Aug 16th.
[07:04] Claire Mendoza: That timeline is doable. Typical flow: 1 week to get creds and network setup, 1 week for SDK/adapter integration and smoke tests, then bench and 1-week pilot. So kickoff the week of Aug 16 fits.
[07:16] Priya Rao: A question on encryption in transit: do you support mTLS between sidecar and Redwood control plane?
[07:22] Devon Park: Yes, mTLS is supported for Private deployments and optional for Dedicated. Hosted supports TLS with client certs for certain enterprise plans.
[07:33] Luis Ortega: For our perf bench, what tooling do you recommend? We can give sample payloads — do you have a recommended harness?
[07:40] Devon Park: We usually run k6 for concurrency and a small python harness for token-level metrics. I'll run a bench from our side against your sample and share raw logs plus a CSV of latency/cost breakdown.
[07:52] Tom Bolton: Regarding fallback policies: if hosted is saturated, can we failover to a smaller, cheaper model automatically?
[07:58] Devon Park: Yes — routing policies can map to fallback chains. For example: preferred=high-quality-llm, fallback=quantized-lowcost-variant. We also support gradual degrade by switching to summary-only responses.
[08:11] Maya Chen: Are there any known limits on embedding dimensionality or vector store compatibility we should be aware of?
[08:17] Devon Park: We support standard vector dims up to 4096; for very large dims we recommend dedicated pools. We have connectors for FAISS, Pinecone, and you can stream embeddings into your own vector service.
[08:30] Claire Mendoza: Okay quick pause — I want to confirm action items and next steps. Devon will run the bench; I'll send pricing and topology docs; Priya will send compliance Qs; Arboretum will provide sample payloads and a list of routes to test.
[08:43] Priya Rao: I'll also send the specific data categories that can't leave our VPC.
[08:47] Luis Ortega: We'll aim to get sample payloads by Aug 6.
[08:50] Claire Mendoza: Great. Any final questions before we wrap?
[08:54] Tom Bolton: One small detail: can we get an export of per-token cost logic so finance can model spend?
[08:59] Claire Mendoza: Yes we'll include the cost model CSV — tokens, encoder/decoder split, and expected per-token microcost for both hosted and dedicated.
[09:09] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Sounds good — excited to try the pilot.
[09:12] Claire Mendoza: Thanks — we'll follow up with the packet shortly.
[09:15] (meeting ends)
